# Riskium

Riskium is a general conceptual ontology for organizing **ecosystem and enterprise risk knowledge**. A **RiskCase** is an identifiable risk item for analysis and tracking relative to objectives and context; it may represent a threat or opportunity from a stated perspective. Register entries, scenarios, occurrences, assessments and evidence describe related aspects without replacing its identity. Formal organizational approval is a local application-profile condition, not a universal existence requirement.

**Published source:** [v0.3.9](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/releases/tag/v0.3.9) · **conceptual model and OWL:** 0.3.2 · **published reader:** 0.4.9 · **explicit-data task profile:** 0.1.0 · **author-held article candidate:** 7.2.21. The article is supplied separately and retains its selected source/evidence bindings; it is not a release asset.

[Pages guide](https://arazsaiearasi3.github.io/riskium/current/index.html) · [Complete concept dictionary](https://arazsaiearasi3.github.io/riskium/current/concepts/index.html) · [Wiki](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/wiki) · [Six verified downloads](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/releases/tag/v0.3.9)

## Current scientific source

The authoritative catalog is [ontology/0.3.2/riskium-model.json](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/ontology/0.3.2/riskium-model.json), with its [native OntoUML exchange](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/ontology/0.3.2/riskium.ontouml.json), [bounded OWL/Turtle projection](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/ontology/0.3.2/riskium.owl.ttl) and [export contract](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/ontology/0.3.2/source-contract.json). The reader covers **82 catalog concepts in eleven subdomains plus one external anchor**. These subdomains organize one general domain; pharmaceutical literature supplies a development context.

This source implements the adopted analytical RiskCase meaning, grounded contextual EvidenceItem use and explicit criterion-based generalization sets. Shared meanings and identifiers remain stable while local profiles add readiness and governance requirements. [The core/profile design decision](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/docs/design/semantic-core-and-application-profiles.md) explains this balance.

## Source-bound evidence

[Actual CI 42776380967](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/actions/runs/42776380967) freshly matched **20 declared selected-source expectations**, then passed **17 separate packaging guard tests**. These are distinct evidence populations. All **six public assets** were independently downloaded and verified against the exact qualified source. [The publication record](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/evaluation/releases/v0.3.9/publication.json) reports public availability; [R2a](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/evaluation/releases/v0.3.9/R2a-outcome.md) retains the earlier preparation receipt.

Package v0.3.9 has six active component families and 32 historical references, binding 1,213 selected files in a 2,091-file source archive. This supports specified structural, logical, data-task and packaging behavior. It is not a whole-model semantic-correctness percentage, optimal-modularity result or production/PostgreSQL claim. Riskium complements related work and makes no superiority claim.

## Historical artifacts and open research

Root model 0.3.1, its native/OWL views, historical SQL/corpus fixtures and prior receipts retain their original source roles. [Retained visualizations](https://arazsaiearasi3.github.io/riskium/current/guide/Visualization.html) identify their model explicitly. Use the current dictionary and 0.3.2 formal files for the successor. The [earlier eighty-concept external-definition review](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/blob/main/documentation/0.4.8/concepts/External-Definitions.md) remains documentary evidence for its own population; broader curation remains [#85](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/issues/85).

Bounded synthetic SQLite/RDF slices exercise selected identity/history and evidence-use tasks. They do not migrate the full database or operationally admit historical withheld pharmaceutical candidates. Full mappings, SQLite/PostgreSQL implementation, dataset reconstruction, [independent semantic review #23](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/issues/23), [semantic modules/COH/COP #77](https://github.com/ArazSaieArasi3/riskium/issues/77) and product/application evaluation remain in the [work plan](https://arazsaiearasi3.github.io/riskium/current/guide/Work-Plan.html).
